Santos FC is incorporating APS – Acqua Performance System into its high-performance structure, a methodology developed by Pai e Filho Assessoria, a national benchmark in large-scale and collective-use swimming pools. Created specifically for high-performance sport, APS establishes a new concept of care for the aquatic environment, geared toward athletes' training, recovery, and preparation routines.

Unlike conventional pool treatment, APS starts from an athlete-focused perspective. The methodology combines highly precise chemical management, continuous monitoring of water parameters, automation, filtration efficiency, and complementary technologies, aiming to provide a more controlled aquatic environment suited to the demands of a high-performance sports routine.

One of the system's main focuses is eliminating factors associated with respiratory, eye, and skin discomfort, especially in athletes subjected to frequent exposure to the pool.

The APS proposal is based on the principle that an aquatic environment developed specifically for high performance helps give athletes better conditions to train, carry out their recovery processes, and reach their full potential. By reducing factors that cause discomfort and more precisely controlling water conditions, the methodology seeks to improve the quality and consistency of training. Better preparation conditions allow athletes to get more out of each session and, as a result, contribute to the development of their sports performance.

With more than 30 years of experience in collective-use pools, Pai e Filho Assessoria developed APS based on the knowledge accumulated in the operation and management of large aquatic facilities. The methodology is intended exclusively for training centers and environments linked to high-performance sport.

At CT Rei Pelé, the work will be applied to the aquatic facilities used by Santos FC athletes, incorporating technical monitoring and precise control of parameters related to water quality.

"In high-performance sport, details matter. Athletes work every day to reach their maximum potential, and our goal is to make water another element designed to support that process. APS was born precisely from this vision: looking at the pool not just as a facility, but as part of the athlete's preparation and recovery environment," explains Nikolas Ladeia, director of Pai e Filho Assessoria.

The arrival of APS at CT Rei Pelé marks the partnership between Santos FC and Pai e Filho Assessoria, bringing into the athletes' daily routine a methodology developed specifically to bring together water, recovery, and high performance.

articles.title: Fatal flaw that will doom Orioles' AL Wild Card chances
articles.summary: The Baltimore Orioles have reached the point where opportunity and urgency are inseparable. They sit at 69–70, 1.5 games behind the Cleveland Guardians for t...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles have reached the point where opportunity and urgency are inseparable. They sit at 69–70, 1.5 games behind the Cleveland Guardians for the final American League Wild Card, with 23 games remaining. The Texas Rangers share Baltimore's record and own the head-to-head tiebreaker, so the Orioles are effectively chasing two clubs.

A 7–3 stretch over their last 10 games has kept them in the playoff race. With that said, Tuesday's 4–2 loss to the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field also displayed how quickly progress can stall. The Orioles possess enough power and improved pitching to threaten everyone ahead of them. Yet their margin has become too thin for an offense that repeatedly wastes plate appearances. The club's fatal flaw is a strikeout-heavy lineup that cannot turn its power and patience into dependable run production.

Orioles power cannot erase empty plate appearances

Baltimore's case as a legitimate contender begins with an offense that has produced more than its overall slash line suggests. The Orioles have scored 630 runs while averaging 4.53 runs per game. They also hit the ball with authority. Through August 31, their 42.8 percent hard-hit rate and 89.9 mph average exit velocity both exceeded league averages.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Pete Alonso gives that approach a formidable center. He entered September batting .268 with a .360 on-base percentage and .500 slugging percentage. His 32 home runs and 141 wRC+ make him a reliable middle-order threat. Baltimore also owns a 9.9 percent walk rate, evidence that this is not simply a reckless lineup.

Those strengths make the weakness more frustrating. The Orioles carried a .235/.317/.397 line and a .714 OPS that ranked 20th in baseball, despite hitting 169 homers and drawing 520 walks. Their 1,281 strikeouts were the fourth-most in the majors. Through August, the Orioles had struck out in 24.4 percent of their regular season plate appearances, compared with a 22.1 percent major-league rate.

The underlying profile explains the contradiction. Baltimore chased fewer pitches than average, but its 26.5 percent whiff rate exceeded the league mark. Its zone-contact rate also fell below average. The Orioles often identify a hittable pitch, attack it and still miss.

That pattern creates an offense built for bursts instead of stability. A walk and one decisive swing can change a game, but consecutive strikeouts can erase the same opportunity. The problem has survived the recent winning stretch. Baltimore posted a .699 OPS in 41 second-half games through August 31, yet went 23–18 because its staff ERA improved to 3.86. Better pitching has covered the lineup's 2026 struggles. It has not cured the problem.

A punishing schedule will magnify every missed chance

That imbalance becomes dangerous because Baltimore cannot afford to wait for its underlying metrics to translate into better results. Nineteen of the club's final 23 games come against teams currently holding playoff spots or direct Wild Card rivals. Its remaining opponents own a combined .517 winning percentage, giving the Orioles the seventh-hardest schedule in baseball. The Guardians, Rangers and Toronto Blue Jays all face easier closing paths.

The Guardians matter most. They hold the final spot, prevent runs more effectively, and put far more balls in play. Cleveland has struck out 170 fewer times than Baltimore. The Orioles must sweep their September 7–9 series to claim the season tiebreaker. Anything less gives Cleveland another advantage if the clubs finish even.

The Rangers have 103 fewer strikeouts and already own the tiebreaker over the Orioles. Toronto trails Baltimore by one game but has struck out 277 fewer times and leads their season series. The Minnesota Twins sit another game back with more runs, a better OPS, and 181 fewer strikeouts. The Orioles cannot assume every challenger will fade while it waits for a timely homer.

Deadline trades also make Baltimore's full-season strikeout rate look more favorable than its current lineup. Adley Rutschman and Taylor Ward combined for 790 Orioles plate appearances while posting strikeout rates of 14.1 and 20.4 percent, respectively.

Jordan Westburg is out for the season, while Ryan Mountcastle and Tyler O'Neill remain sidelined. Luis Robert Jr. and Heston Kjerstad add upside, but neither carries enough current major-league certainty to promise an instant transformation.

Baltimore is 16–19 in one-run games, where a productive out can matter as much as a home run. Strikeouts do not advance runners or force defenses to execute. Against better opponents, those empty plate appearances will turn competitive starts into avoidable losses. Reaching 83 wins requires a 14–9 finish, and even that may not overcome unfavorable tiebreakers.

The strongest counterargument offers real hope. Baltimore's expected average, slugging percentage, and wOBA exceeded actual results. Headed into the last month of the regular season, Robert adds upside, Alonso remains a proven anchor , and the pitching staff has improved. The Orioles' recent record shows they can win during offensive lulls.

Expected production, however, cannot recover a strikeout or extend the schedule. Baltimore must put more strikes in play, sustain rallies, and give its pitchers a steadier scoring floor. Power should become the finishing tool instead of the entire plan. If the pattern of walks, hard contact, and too many empty swings continues, the Orioles' fatal flaw will close their path to October before their upside can rescue them.

articles.title: Zverev out-lasts Sonego in wild five-setter to advance at US Open
articles.summary: Top-seeded Alexander Zverev scraped into the second round of the US Open on Tuesday, beating 89th-ranked Lorenzo Sonego 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (7/9), 7-5, 6-4.A love...
articles.body:
Top-seeded Alexander Zverev scraped into the second round of the US Open on Tuesday, beating 89th-ranked Lorenzo Sonego 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (7/9), 7-5, 6-4.

Zverev fought off a determined challenge from Sonego in a tense all-court battle spiced by unlikely retrievals, impossibly angled winners and some inexplicable errors, which wrapped up on Arthur Ashe Stadium after four hours and 53 minutes at 1:55 in the morning.

"I'm just happy I won, that's it," Zverev said. "Incredible battle, a lot of up and downs -- nearly five hours for a first round, I think it's the longest first round match I ever played in my life.

"Credit to him, he played an incredible match," Zverev said, adding it was just the kind of battle he needed after lackluster performances in two hard court tournaments coming into the Open.

Zverev, who followed his first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros with a Wimbledon final appearance, notched his seventh win in as many matches against Sonego.

He avoided becoming the first men's top seed in 23 years to fall in the first round of Grand Slam, booking a second-round meeting with France's Quentin Halys.

After fending off a break point early in the fifth set, Zverev broke for 3-2 lead -- aided by two unforced errors and a double-fault from Sonego.

The German had pocketed the first set without facing a break point. After surrendering a break in the seventh game Sonego made him work to close it out, saving four set points on his own serve in the ninth game before Zverev produced a love hold.

The pressure built in the second set, Sonego earning his first break of the match for a 5-3 lead and serving it out to level the match.

Zverev looked first frustrated and then dejected as his errors piled up in the third set.

Sonego gave himself a break chance in the seventh game with a defensive lob that left the German stranded, and Zverev dropped his serve meekly with his second double fault of the game.

Sonego was serving for the set at 5-4 when Zverev stepped it up, breaking the Italian at love in a game that opened with Zverev's pinpoint passing winner off an acrobatic volley from Sonego.

Level again they went to the tiebreaker, where Zverev surrendered the set with a double fault on Sonego's second set point.

Sonego saved a pair of break points to open the fourth set and had saved three more in the fifth game before Zverev broke for 3-2, seizing the advantage with a lunging cross-court backhand that Sonego couldn't reach.

The momentum was short-lived as Sonego broke back in the next game, taking advantage of Zverev's botched overhead and closing out the game with a stunning passing shot and a forehand volley.

A love hold then put Sonego up 4-3, but he couldn't hang on, he fought off four more break points in the ninth game but Zverev broke him for 6-5 lead on the way to forcing the fifth set.

articles.title: David Sánchez avisa sobre Julián Álvarez y el Barça: "Volveremos a hablar en el siguiente mercado"

articles.summary: El presentador de 'DSF' asegura en La Tribu que Laporta sigue "empecinado" en que el delantero argentino sea el heredero de Lewandowski
articles.body: El mercado de fichajes ha cerrado sus puertas y Julián Álvarez continúa en el Atlético de Madrid, pero David Sánchez tiene claro que el futuro del delantero argentino volverá a convertirse en uno de los grandes asuntos de mercado. En sus Picotazos de La Tribu, el periodista ha advertido de que el interés del Barcelona sigue intacto. "Se cierra el mercado de fichajes. Carpetazo, por tanto, al tema de Julián Álvarez y el FC Barcelona. El argentino sigue en el Atlético de Madrid", comenzó David Sánchez, que no da por terminado el culebrón pese a que finalmente no se haya producido ningún movimiento. El periodista dejó abierta la puerta a que la situación vuelva a ponerse sobre la mesa próximamente: "Veremos si cumpliendo sus años de contrato o volvemos a hablar del futuro de Julián Álvarez en el mercado de invierno y sobre todo en el siguiente mercado de verano". Según David Sánchez, el presidente azulgrana no ha cambiado de idea respecto al delantero del Atlético: "Joan Laporta sigue empecinado en que el argentino sea el heredero de Lewandowski en el FC Barcelona". Además, señaló que esa idea no sería únicamente del máximo mandatario azulgrana: "Hansi Flick y Deco piensan lo mismo que el presidente". David Sánchez también fue contundente al referirse a la posición de Fernando Hidalgo y del propio futbolista: "Fernando Hidalgo y sobre todo Julián Álvarez siguen teniendo la clara intención y única intención de dejar el Atlético de Madrid para recalar en el Barça". Por todo ello, David Sánchez considera que el asunto regresará tarde o temprano a la actualidad. "Hoy ponemos punto y final a este culebrón sabiendo perfectamente que volveremos a hablar de Julián, el Atlético y el Barça en el siguiente mercado de fichajes", sentenció.

articles.title: El Desafío Santalucía arranca en Vietnam: "Ha sido una pájara tremenda"
articles.standfirst: José Puch sufre en la primera etapa de montaña que sacan con nota Pilar, Rafa, Pablo y Quique
articles.summary: José Puch sufre en la primera etapa de montaña que sacan con nota Pilar, Rafa, Pablo y Quique
articles.body: Hay lugares en el mundo en los que los desafíos se pintan con los mejores paisajes. Vietnam es uno de ellos: entre arrozales y montañas arranca la tercera edición del Desafío Santalucía para seniors, mayores de 65 años que afrontan la aventura de sus vidas a más de 10.000 kilómetros de sus casas. Pilar (79 años), Quique (78), Pablo (70), José (69) y Rafa (67) empiezan a dar las primeras pedaladas del Desafío en Mai Chau, una zona de arrozales y montañas al suroeste de Hanoi donde el tiempo parece detenerse. Aquí la vida va más lenta, como el acompasado baile sobre la bicicleta de estos cinco seniors que afrontan la primera de las tres etapas ciclistas antes de abordar el trekking, paddle SUP, rápel y espeleología que completarán este Desafío Santalucia por tierras vietnamitas. Zuriñe Rodríguez, triatleta olímpica española en Londres 2012, dirige la expedición y pronto detecta que alguien flaquea en el equipo. Mientras Rafa vuela y Quique, Pablo y Pilar van a buen ritmo, al fondo del grupo José Puch no responde tras un golpe de calor. "No me siento bien", comenta el madrileño, quien pese a intentarlo no puede más y tiene que poner pie en tierra. Llega caminando a la cima de esta primera etapa mientras sus compañeros le esperan y le animan: "Ha sido una pájara tremenda", reconoce exhausto a la vez que se hidrata, toma aire y descansa antes de subirse otra vez a la bici para seguir el recorrido. El espíritu de equipo prevalece en este Desafío Santalucia y todos se agrupan para afrontar lo que resta de una etapa en la que la humedad es elevada e hidratarse empieza a ser una obligación. Todos arropan a José con el fin de llevarle al final de etapa. Queda mucho por delante, pero la sensación es que ya ha pasado lo peor. La carretera se va estrechando mientras las montañas aparecen a ambos lados y cientos de banderas ondean en el camino recordando que Vietnam es una república comunista que ha abrazado el capitalismo y que es de los países que más crece del mundo (8%) emulando el modelo de su vecina China. "No nos dio tiempo a disfrutar del descenso porque íbamos muy pendientes de la carretera tan estrecha y temíamos salirnos", cuenta Pilar. "Yo me sentí mucho mejor bajando y la pájara se me empezó a pasar", afirma José recordando cómo fue su dura etapa. En pleno descenso, al lado de los caminos de tierra aparece un verde intenso, casi irreal. Son los arrozales. Se extienden por las montañas como terrazas dibujadas a mano. Solo cuando el terreno se allana, los cinco componentes del equipo se relajan y se dejan llevar hasta la meta. "Hemos disfrutado mucho esta etapa", reconocen los valencianos Rafa y Quique recordando los casi 50 kilómetros recorridos con un desnivel de 747 metros. Y es que aunque tengan entre 68 y 79 años todos han demostrado que la edad no es una frontera para cumplir sus sueños en esta maravillosa tierra vietnamita donde no solo se trata de llegar sino de disfrutar del camino. Mañana más y mejor.

articles.title: Paredes puts question mark over Argentina future
articles.summary: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes says it is going to be "difficult" for him to continue playing for his country in the wake of his 10-match international...
articles.body:
Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes says it is going to be "difficult" for him to continue playing for his country in the wake of his 10-match international ban.

Paredes received the suspension from Fifa for his part in an on-pitch confrontation following Argentina's 1-0 defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.

The 32-year-old grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground, before appearing to strike the latter in the face.

Paredes also suggested Argentina legend Lionel Messi retiring from international football could play a part in his decision.

"It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team," said Boca Juniors player Paredes.

"Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

"I haven't discussed it with the coach [Lionel Scaloni] yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make."

Messi, 39, recently announced his retirement from international football, saying he had "nothing left to give" having "given it my all".

He captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022 but could not repeat the feat against Spain in his final game for his country.

Messi scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina to become his country's all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.

"Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled," Paredes added.

"We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us."

articles.title: Puka Nacua's ex-girlfriend Hallie Aiono details "extreme betrayal" in new video
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is still being investigated by the NFL before Week 1, and new personal news about him came out on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is still being investigated by the NFL before Week 1, and new personal news about him came out on Tuesday.

Jessica Cryderman - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) during Rams training camp at the Loyola Marymount University on Monday, July 27th in Westchester, CA.

Hallie Aiono and Nacua met at BYU and started dating in 2021. They were together for about four years. In June, before having her baby in October, Aiono went to court to prove Nacua is the father, ask for custody, and get child support.

They have broken up, and Aiono is now sharing details about her pregnancy and their past relationship. As the court/NFL decision is still pending, his ex-girlfriend Hallie Aiono has shared serious allegations about their time together.

"I went from loving somebody so deeply for four years, I felt it in my bones, to experiencing extreme betrayal, abuse, complete neglect from them, in what felt like it happened almost overnight," she said.

Aiono shared her story in a TikTok video on Sunday night, but she did not name Nacua or directly accuse him of anything.

"I've talked about it on here a few other times, but I have experienced the darkest darkest days of my life in the past year and a half," she added. "And I have healed so much. I really have."

Nacua is also dealing with a lawsuit from Madison Atiabi, who claims he bit her shoulder at a New Year's Eve party. Atiabi's attorney, Joseph Kar, told the New York Post :

"I don't know if you know," Kar said, "but the mouth is one of the dirtiest places on the planet given the amount of bacteria we have as humans. . . . My client has also suffered severe emotional distress and mental anguish and is being treated."

Additionally, Nacua apologized for making an offensive gesture targeting Jewish people during a live video after people criticized him.

"When I appeared the other day on a social media livestream, it was suggested to me to perform a specific movement as part of my next touchdown celebration," he said. "At the time, I had no idea this act was antisemitic in nature and perpetuated harmful stereotypes against Jewish people."

Until the NFL makes a final ruling, fantasy football players must keep an eye on whether Puka Nacua will play in the Rams' first game against the San Francisco 49ers on September 10.

articles.title: Tyson Fury confirms Anthony Joshua fight at NYC’s Madison Square Garden
articles.summary: No date has been set for the all-British heavyweight boxing showdown, but it is expected to be held in November.
articles.body:
Former world heavyweight champion Tyson ⁠⁠⁠⁠Fury has confirmed that his long-awaited heavyweight boxing showdown with fellow Briton Anthony Joshua will take place at New York City’s iconic Madison Square Garden.

No exact date has been set for the Joshua vs Fury fight — one of the biggest in British boxing history — although it is expected to be held in November after both signed a contract with Turki Alalshikh, Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority chairman.

“What a place, what a venue, what a fight,” Fury said in a post on Instagram.

Fury called New York City “the land of opportunity”, but fans criticised him in comments on the post as they questioned why an all-British fight was being held in the US, and not at a location like Wembley Stadium in the United Kingdom.

Fury, who ⁠⁠⁠⁠turned 38 in August, has won 36 ⁠⁠⁠⁠professional bouts, suffering his ⁠⁠⁠⁠only losses in two fights with Ukraine’s Oleksandr Usyk in 2024. He announced his return to boxing in January, having retired from the sport in December 2024 after losing to Usyk in a bout for three of the four major world titles.

Joshua and Fury were unable to agree on terms in 2021, and plans for the face-off fell apart after a US judge ruled Fury had to face Deontay Wilder in a trilogy fight instead.

In the lead-up to the Joshua showdown, Fury forced Polish opponent Mariusz Wach to retire in a tune-up ⁠⁠⁠⁠bout in July attended by some 1,500 fans at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Pattaya, Thailand.

articles.title: Yankees news: Aaron Boone reveals what’s behind Spencer Jones’ success vs. lefties
articles.summary: The New York Yankees lineup has become notoriously lefty-heavy, and right fielder Spencer Jones, who is establishing himself as an everyday player in his fi...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees lineup has become notoriously lefty-heavy, and right fielder Spencer Jones, who is establishing himself as an everyday player in his first season in the big leagues, is another southpaw. However, Jones' righty/lefty splits isn't that debilitating for the Yankees to the point that they need to put him in a platoon. In fact, the 25-year-old is shining against same-handed pitching, and he took it one step further in their 7-3 win over the Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday.

Jones began the night in the most ideal way possible. He tagged Angels starter Grayson Rodriguez for a two-run home run that set the tone for the Yankees in the top of the first inning, and New York never trailed in the game. He went 1-2 against Rodriguez with a walk, and even when the Angels deployed three lefty relievers, that scarcely did anything to slow Jones down.

Jones, against lefties Samy Natera Jr. and Sammy Peralta, went 1-1 from the plate with a walk. He's now 14-35 from the plate against southpaws, which is good for a batting average of exactly .400. Suffice to say, the Yankees are very happy with what they're seeing from the 25-year-old right fielder, and manager Aaron Boone shed light on what is fueling Jones' success as of late.

"He's doing great. He's benefitting from his experience up here and applying it. I've talked about him having aptitude, and that's what he seems to have. He's taking the things he's experiencing every day at this level and putting them into practice. He's doing an outstanding job," Boone said in his postgame presser, via YES Network on X.

Jones, on the season, now has nine home runs and 28 runs batted in on an OPS of .771. It speaks volumes to the trust the Yankees have in him that he was batting cleanup on Tuesday, and he did more than repay Boone's faith in him.

articles.title: Dave Roberts wants Dodgers to 'flush this one' after Cardinals loss
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers came home Tuesday night hoping to turn the page.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers came home Tuesday night hoping to turn the page.

Instead, they were reminded just how quickly a game can get away from them.

After a six-game road trip, the Dodgers returned to Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium and were overwhelmed early, falling behind by seven runs through the first three innings before ultimately losing 13-8 to the St. Louis Cardinals.

The loss dropped the Dodgers to 82-56 and opened a nine-game homestand on a sour note. The Dodgers' offense eventually found its footing, but the deficit created by a rough night from the pitching staff was simply too much to overcome.

The Dodgers allowed five home runs, with Cardinals' Thomas Saggese doing much of the damage. Saggese entered the night hitting .210 with one home run and four RBIs.

He left with three home runs and seven RBIs.

For the Dodgers, the problem wasn't necessarily an inability to swing the bat. It was everything that happened before the offense could get comfortable.

The left-hander lasted only three innings, allowing eight hits and seven earned runs while walking one and striking out two on 63 pitches. It marked his worst start as a Dodger and put the Dodgers in a hole it would spend the rest of the night trying to escape.

The Cardinals wasted little time getting to him.

Ramon Urias opened the scoring with a home run before Saggese followed with one of his own, giving St. Louis a 2-0 lead in the second inning.

Saggese struck again in the third, and the Cardinals continued piling on as the Dodgers struggled to contain the hard contact.

Lauer acknowledged afterward that he may have overcomplicated things.

"Sometimes you can go a little too far and kind of lose yourself," Lauer said.

He believes he has been tinkering too much and wasn't able to make the necessary adjustments once the game began moving in the wrong direction.

"Getting back to the basics is really, really all I think I need to do," Lauer said.

His night ended after the third inning, with Seth Halvorsen taking over in the fourth.

And by then, the Cardinals had already built a 7-0 advantage.

The game could have easily turned into a complete blowout. It didn't.

Mookie Betts reached base four times and drove in all four of the Dodgers' first runs, delivering an RBI double in the third inning before adding another RBI double in the fifth.

One of those early runs came courtesy of a defensive miscue by St. Louis.

A shallow fly ball turned into an adventure when Jose Fermin and Jordan Walker collided in right field, allowing Betts' pop-up to fall and three Dodgers runs to cross the plate.

It wasn't pretty, but the Dodgers finally had some life.

Then came the moment Dodgers fans had been waiting nearly three months to see.

After missing nearly three months with an injury, Smith returned Tuesday and immediately looked comfortable at the plate.

He went 1-for-5 with a double, two RBIs and a run scored, including an RBI hit that gave the Dodgers another spark as they attempted to climb back into the game.

Smith said afterward that the injury simply needed time to heal.

"It was just an injury that needed time to heal," Smith said. "Felt good. Felt like I didn't miss a beat."

Dave Roberts liked what he saw from his catcher, particularly considering the amount of time Smith had missed.

"He took good AB's considering he hasn't played a long time," Roberts said. "Good to see him with that workload up, he'll be back on Thursday."

Smith will get Wednesday off before returning to the lineup Thursday.

Even with the offense fighting, the Cardinals kept answering.

By the time the Dodgers reached the late innings, St. Louis had pushed its lead to 13-5.

The Dodgers managed to make the final score respectable, but the three-run ninth inning merely changed the appearance of the game rather than its story.

Tommy Edman collected his third hit of the night and drove in another run in the ninth, cutting the deficit to 13-8.

That was as close as the Dodgers would get.

The Dodgers' offense had produced enough moments to keep the team engaged, but not enough to erase the enormous hole created by the pitching staff.

"From the day, there were some positives with the AB's," Roberts said. "I liked some of the swings, taking the walks, pushing runs across."

"But tonight, we got behind. Eric wasn't sharp, a lot of hard contact. We had a tough start but it was good to see us fighting."

And perhaps most importantly, Roberts appreciated that the Dodgers didn't simply fold.

"Our guys didn't quit, which I really appreciate."

The timing of the loss makes it more concerning than simply dropping the first game of a homestand.

The Dodgers entered September hoping to leave their August struggles behind. Instead, they surrendered 13 runs to a Cardinals team that came into the night below .500.

The Dodgers now sit at 82-56, three and a half games behind the Milwaukee Brewers and only a half-game ahead of the Atlanta Braves in the National League.

With 24 games remaining, there isn't much room left for games to get away like Tuesday did.

The Dodgers have already lost the tiebreaker to both Atlanta and Milwaukee, making every remaining game increasingly important.

The offense can survive an occasional off night.

What the Dodgers can't afford is for its pitching to repeatedly put the team in impossible situations before the bats have a chance to respond.

Five Cardinals home runs. Seven runs allowed through three innings. A 13-run night from St. Louis.

And ultimately, another loss at a time when the Dodgers desperately need to start stacking wins.

The Dodgers have Yoshinobu Yamamoto scheduled to start Wednesday, followed by Tarik Skubal on Thursday, giving the Dodgers an opportunity to quickly erase the memory of Tuesday's collapse.

Roberts said he remains confident the Dodgers can still win the series.

"Try to flush this one and win tomorrow night, and give ourselves a chance to win the series," Roberts said.

The Dodgers didn't lose Tuesday because their offense stopped competing. They lost because their pitching dug a hole far too deep to escape.

Roberts said the team had a "good hitters meeting" earlier in the day, and the offense showed signs of life despite the deficit.

But as September begins, the Dodgers need more than signs. They need results.

As for Shohei Ohtani, Roberts said his right arm "feels pretty good" and expressed no immediate concern about Ohtani's knee or the hit by pitch.

For one night, though, the biggest concern was much more straightforward:

articles.body:
Week 0 is in the rear-view mirror, and Week 1's arrival is imminent. Of the 18 teams in the conference, only USC took the field in Week 0. The result was an easy victory over San Jose State. I predicted how USC will fare in its other 11 games, and did the same for every Big Ten team. Along with win-loss projections, I leave you with three predictions ahead of the college football season.

The first is that the national champion won't come from the Big Ten or the SEC. I like the Miami Hurricanes.

The second is that the Heisman Trophy winner will be a running back. You probably guessed it, give me Miami's star running back Mark Fletcher.

The third is that Oregon won't reach the Big Ten Championship Game. But it'll be the team that Miami beats in the national title game.

Wins: North Texas, Howard, WKU, Northwestern, at Rutgers, at Nebraska, Ohio State, Minnesota, USC, at Washington, Purdue

I am a big believer in Indiana because Curt Cignetti is the best football coach in the sport. I respect the two national championships Kirby Smart has won at Georgia, but nobody in the sport could've executed what Cignetti has in Bloomington thus far. It's not a rebuild. A rebuild suggests that the program was once worth talking about. Indiana was a bottom dweller in the Big Ten, and now it's fresh off a national championship. If you think Cignetti is going to have a drop off, well, I have bad news for you. Fernando Mendoza now resides in Las Vegas, and the pressure is now on TCU transfer Josh Hoover's shoulders. The thing about Cignetti is that he's been sensational at finding perfect plug-and-play guys, so I think Hoover will excel.

Indiana's toughest game on the schedule is Ohio State, but it's a home game. It will be the best environment that stadium has ever seen and the wild amounts of alcoholic beverages will be consumed by Hoosier fans as they celebrate another victory over the Buckeyes. One week later, Indiana suffers its lone regular season defeat at the hands of Michigan on the road.

The way I see it, Ohio State is the best team in the Big Ten. It might be the best team in the country. Some will argue Oregon, but the Buckeyes have the nation's best player in Jeremiah Smith and a head coach in Ryan Day that has won a national championship. While Dan Lanning is certainly on the right track at Oregon, his inability to win when it matters most has left the Ducks on the wrong end of blowout CFP losses the last two seasons. Those two teams meet Nov. 7 and I think the Buckeyes beat the Ducks, and every other team not coached by Curt Cignetti. The head-to-head loss to Indiana will give the Hoosiers the tiebreaker, so Ohio State finishes No. 2 in the standings but has a shot at redemption as the two square off in the Big Ten Championship Game for the second straight season.

I got this far without mentioning the Texas game. Whoops. I'm not sure how I feel about Texas. I've expected an SEC Championship the last two years and it hasn't happened yet. I think Ohio State is better coached and I think it handles the daunting a raucous crowd in another low scoring rock fight.

Wins: Ball State, at Texas, Kent State, Illinois, at Iowa, Maryland, at USC, Oregon, Northwestern, at Nebraska, Michigan

Oregon fans have been saying it forever. This is the year. You know what? Maybe they have a point. The Ducks have immense depth and return its signal caller Dante Moore, who could be in for a Heisman Trophy worthy season. Under Lanning, Oregon has been a wrecking ball in the regular season and I think that continues this season as most teams just don't have the roster or depth to match up well for 60 minutes. Of course, what matters most for Oregon is what happens after the regular season concludes. Can the Ducks finally climb the mountain and stand atop college football? History suggests no. Experts predict yes. Oregon's lone defeat will be to Ohio State. The tiebreaker puts the Buckeyes ahead of the Ducks, who get extra rest before the College Football Playoff.

Wins: Boise State, at Oklahoma State, Portland State, at USC, UCLA, Nebraska, at Illinois, Northwestern, Michigan, at Michigan State, Washington

It's easy to laugh at USC. The constant hype that ends with disappointing seasons. The lackluster environment. The fall from grace. Enjoy it while you can, USC's campaign won't be humorous. Lincoln Riley needs to have a breakthrough season and get the Trojans to the College Football Playoff and a 9-3 record as a Big Ten program should be enough to get there. The key for the Trojans is avoiding bad losses. Perhaps the most important game on the schedule, aside from the obvious three, comes against Washington in what could end up being a win-and-in game when the College Football Playoff committee is reviewing the body of work for teams on the bubble. To me, that game is a coinflip. I think Riley is a better coach than Jedd Fisch, so I give the Trojans a tiny edge in that game. If it were in Seattle, my pick would be the Huskies. The win that feels like Riley has turned the corner will come on the road against Penn State.

Wins: San Jose State, Fresno State, Louisiana, at Rutgers, Washington, at Penn State, at Wisconsin, Maryland, at UCLA

After tracking wins and losses, I was surprised that I had Penn State at 9-3. Then I checked the wins and thought, "wow, this is an easy schedule." Penn State is looking to work its way back into a contender following the firing of James Franklin and first-year head coach Matt Campbell is the man tasked with doing it. Making matters easier is his familiarity with several newcomers that followed him from Iowa State, including quarterback Rocco Becht. I don't see the Nittany Lions walking into Husky stadium and leaving victorious, and beating Michigan on the road feels like an equally tall task. So, the defining games on the schedule are home games against USC and Minnesota. I predict they'll split those games, but winning both would leave the Nittany Lions as two-loss team in my projection.

Wins: Marshall, at Temple, Buffalo, Wisconsin, at Northwestern, Purdue, Minnesota, Rutgers, at Maryland

Minnesota's schedule is pretty manageable as well. The biggest obstacle will be its road trips. All three of its losses will come on the road, falling to Washington, Indiana and Penn State. But it'll pick up a pivotal road win against Wisconsin and go undefeated at home, including a victory over Michigan. I predicted Minnesota will have the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year in EDGE Anthony Smith. Now here I am predicting the Golden Gophers will be the B1G surprise team in 2026.

Wins: Eastern Illinois, Mississippi State, Akron, Michigan, at Purdue, Iowa, UCLA, Northwestern, at Wisconsin

Losses: at Washington, at Indiana, at Penn State

For a while, Kyle Whittingham was the nation's most underrated coach. One of the Wolverines' defeats will come in a non-conference bout against the Oklahoma Sooners. The other three losses are all road games against Minnesota, Oregon and Ohio State. I was split on the Minnesota bout, but if I'm going to put my faith in the Gophers then I need to stand by it.

Wins: Western Michigan, UTEP, Iowa, Penn State, Indiana, at Rutgers, Michigan State, UCLA

Losses: Oklahoma, at Minnesota, at Oregon, at Ohio State

If Nebraska can beat Washington on Halloween and snap its three-game skid against Iowa on the road, we're looking at a strong season for head coach Matt Rhule. Nebraska handles business against the easiest opponents on its schedule, splits the aforementioned Washington and Iowa bouts. It suffers a frustrating loss to Illinois and drops the toughest games on its schedule against Indiana, Oregon and Ohio State.

Wins: Ohio, Bowling Green, North Dakota, at Michigan State, Maryland, Washington, at Rutgers, at Illinois

Losses: Indiana, at Oregon, at Iowa, Ohio State

I don't think there are eight teams better than Washington in the Big Ten. But hey, that's life in the Big Ten. This conference is loaded with talented teams and I'll need to be wrong about one or two games for the Huskies to make the CFP. Jedd Fisch has built the Huskies into a CFP hopeful and it'll be a major accomplishment if he can do it in his third season at the helm. He has a quarterback capable of winning a Heisman Trophy in Demond Williams, but in order for that to happen, the Huskies will need to establish its rushing attack to take pressure off of their star quarterback. Washington's biggest star on defense won't be on the field this season and while that's typically a bad thing, it's defensive coordinator Ryan Walters who holds the honor. His defense played well against high octane offenses last season, particularly against Ohio State and Oregon, and repeating that success will determine whether or not the Huskies make the CFP.

If you think my prediction is harsh, here's something to consider. Washington has been stellar at home, so an upset over Indiana is certainly a possibility. Do I find it likely? No, because Cignetti is Cignetti. I also feel pretty confident that the Huskies won't match up well with the Ducks on the road. But… Washington vs. USC is a toss-up, and depending on how UW's rushing attack looks early in the season, I might pick UW to win that game. Then there's Nebraska. A blackout under the lights on Halloween in a stadium that holds over 85,000 just does not sound like a fun night of football. However, Washington is the better team, and if it wants to be a CFP team, winning that type of games is how you get there.

Wins: Washington State, Utah State, EWU, Minnesota, Iowa, at Purdue, Penn State, at Michigan State

Losses: at USC, at Nebraska, Indiana, at Oregon

If Iowa loses to Washington and Michigan, beats Nebraska and all four teams finish with the same record, there's a tiebreaker scenario that I'll let the computers worry about. Iowa is the team I feel least confident in of the four so Iowa gets the No. 10 slot. Sounds fair to me! Iowa drops its four toughest games on the schedule against Michigan, Ohio State, Washington and Minnesota, but beats its rival Nebraska for the fourth straight season.

articles.title: Liverpool confirm agreement for £30m signing
articles.summary: Liverpool Sign Lucca Brughmans in £30m Goalkeeper DealLiverpool have moved early and decisively, completing the signing of teenage goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans...
articles.body:
Liverpool Sign Lucca Brughmans in £30m Goalkeeper Deal

Liverpool have moved early and decisively, completing the signing of teenage goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from Genk in a deal worth up to £30m. He is 18, stands at 6ft 7in, and has signed a six-year contract. For now, there is no rush. He will stay at Genk on loan for the rest of this season and arrive at Anfield ahead of the 2027-28 campaign.

This is not a transfer driven by short-term need. It is a calculated investment in a specialist position where timing matters. Goalkeepers develop differently, and Liverpool clearly believe Brughmans has the profile to become a serious first-team option down the line. He has already started all four of Genk's games this season and has represented Belgium at youth level, which tells you there is substance behind the fee.

Lucca Brughmans fits Liverpool succession plan

The headline figure is up to £30m, with add-ons built into the agreement. In simple terms, Liverpool are paying for potential, height, reach and projection. In the modern market, elite young goalkeepers are expensive, particularly when clubs think they can become starters for a decade.

There is also logic in the timing. Liverpool currently have Alisson, Giorgi Mamardashvili, Freddie Woodman and Vitezslav Jaros among their goalkeeping options. Alisson's contract expires next summer, while Mamardashvili's longer-term situation remains unclear. Brughmans gives the club another route, and a potentially high-upside one.

Liverpool recruitment strategy targets elite youth

This deal sits neatly within the club's wider recruitment model. Liverpool's global talent department, led by Matt Newberry, has been active in identifying young players before their value goes through the roof. Earlier this year they brought in Senegal defender Mor Talla N'diaye and Austria defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe after strong displays at the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Goalkeeper Armin Pecsi and midfielder Samuel Martinez have also arrived over the past year from Hungary and Colombia respectively, with Pecsi now out on loan at TSV Hartberg. The pattern is obvious. Liverpool are stockpiling elite youth, backing their scouting, and planning several windows ahead.

Genk goalkeeper arrives with expectation and patience

Brughmans will not be judged immediately, and that suits everyone. Liverpool have bought a prospect, not a finished product. The fee is large, the contract is long, and the pathway is clear. If he develops as expected, this will look smart. If not, £30m for a teenager in goal will invite scrutiny. That is how it works at this level.

articles.title: 'Can't say he faked it, but.....': PCB director Aaqib Javed wants inquiry into Imam-ul-Haq's injury at Lord's
articles.summary: PCB director Aaqib Javed confirmed an inquiry into Imam-ul-Haq after the opener sat out both innings of the Lord's Test with a calf strain.
articles.body:
Aaqib Javed has demanded a formal inquiry into Imam-ul-Haq's calf injury after he failed to bat in either innings at Lord's.

The PCB director defended sending seven players home, blaming Pakistan's management for picking a flawed playing combination.

Misbah-ul-Haq has already quit the selection panel, though Aaqib insists he has no plans to follow him out.

PCB to investigate Imam-ul-Haq's lord's injury: Aaqib Javed promises strict action over opener missing both innings

Pakistan cricket's meltdown just got another twist as PCB director of high performance Aaqib Javed has come out swinging at Imam-ul-Haq for sitting out both innings of the Lord's Test.

Speaking to Pakistani broadcaster Geo, Aaqib didn't mince words about how let down he felt. He said he's "deeply disappointed" in Imam and made clear the player would be facing questions over his call to sit out; a decision put down to a low-grade tear in his left calf. A formal inquiry will be initiated to find out exactly what happened.

Imam was among the seven players the PCB recalled home following Pakistan's 194-run defeat in the second Test, and his decision to sit out drew plenty of criticism along the way.

Just minutes before play resumed on day two, the board issued a statement confirming the calf tear, adding that whether he'd feature again in the match would depend on medical advice. He didn't take any further part over the next two days, though he was seen warming up with the squad on the fourth morning.

"The Imam injury is a big question mark, and a deep disappointment," Aaqib said. "Players in the past used to get injuries, but they used to put on casts and still tried [to play]. We'll take action against this.

"How is it possible that a pulled muscle ruled you out of batting in both innings? He should have tried and fought. He'll have to face an inquiry; I can't say he faked it, but a muscle pull like that cannot stop you from batting altogether."

Aaqib defends mass player recall, slams team selection

Imam and six other players joined him on the flight home, along with head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul, as the PCB tore up much of its touring party. Aaqib explained the thinking behind such a drastic call, saying it was meant to send a clear message to those recalled, while also pointing a finger squarely at team management for what he called poor selection choices.

"Two Test matches have come and gone, and the team has not competed in any way," he said, pointing out that faster options like Ubaid Shah were left out despite being available. "They [the management] had a pace allrounder available, a second wicketkeeper, a fast bowler in Ubaid Shah. But those decisions were not being made."

He revealed he'd personally pushed captain Babar Azam and the coaching staff to include Ubaid, arguing the pace attack lacked variety.

"No batter in our top seven bowls. We should have included an allrounder, but most importantly, get in Ubaid Shah, who bowls close to 140kph," he said, also questioning the choice to stick with Mohammad Rizwan behind the stumps over Ghazi Ghori.

"Someone had to take action. The world is laughing at us because we can't even compete. One fast bowler changes the composition of your attack. I understand dropping [Salman] Agha, who's out of form, but you should have played Ghazi Ghori instead of [Mohammad] Rizwan [as the wicketkeeper]," he said.

"Someone had to take action. The world is laughing at us because we can't even compete. The message we're sending to the recalled players is that you have to raise your game on important tours and compete, and we should be able to see some effort."

Fallout continues as Misbah resigns from selection panel

The criticism hasn't just been aimed downward, though, as Aaqib himself hasn't escaped scrutiny. He's held his post for two years now, a stretch that's seen coaches like Jason Gillespie and Gary Kirsten come and go, and he briefly juggled a coaching role alongside his selection duties too.

He was also part of the group that appointed Sarfaraz just three months back, only to see him removed after a mere six Tests in charge. Misbah-ul-Haq, meanwhile, has already resigned from the selection committee in the wake of the squad shake-up.

Aaqib, however, was firm that he isn't following Misbah's lead, drawing a clear line between the original squad selection and the team's subsequent form collapse.

"When we select the team as coach or captain and make a squad, we're responsible for that squad. But once they go on tour, we cannot do anything about the match-to-match combination," Aaqib said.

"No one doubted these players' performances when selected. But when players are completely out of form, and you're not competing at all, then we needed to make a decision. When you're not making the right decisions despite getting messages conveyed to you to play the right combination [that's a problem]. Your captain, head coach and management have some responsibilities."

Public accusations rarely fix broken systems

There's something deeply uncomfortable about a board director publicly casting doubt on a player's injury without offering any real evidence beyond suspicion. Even hedged with "I can't say he faked it," the accusation lands exactly where it was aimed, and that's a dangerous way for any administrator to operate.

If the PCB believes something's off, that's what medical panels and internal inquiries exist for, not television interviews. What's more telling here is Aaqib's own position: he's been central to the very decisions he's now criticising from a distance, including Sarfaraz's short-lived coaching stint.

Blaming a player's fitness while dodging accountability for having appointed the management now under fire doesn't inspire much confidence. Pakistan cricket doesn't need more finger-pointing from the top; it needs a board willing to look honestly at its own repeated missteps.

articles.title: What should you look out for this Premiership midweek?
articles.summary: With five games on Wednesday and an Edinburgh derby on Thursday, plus a transfer deadline looming, what should you look out for in the Scottish Premiership t...
articles.body:
Only a handful of games into the Scottish Premiership season and it could be argued that about half its team managers are already looking nervously over their shoulders.

At least most do not have to deal with a transfer deadline day before preparing for this midweek's fixtures as the domestic deadline has been delayed until the dust had settled on the five games scheduled for Wednesday evening.

However, while they have another chance to assess their reshaped squads before another hasty round of phone calls and negotiations before the transfer window closes at 17:00 BST on Thursday, Heart of Midlothian and Hibernian have no such luxury as they meet later that evening.

So what should we look out for in that big game - and the five others on Wednesday?

At the start of the campaign you would have imagined there would be no question marks about Martin O'Neill's position after he rescued a league and couple double out of a traumatic season in his second spell as Celtic's interim manager.

However, the veteran Northern Irishman missed last month's win over Kilmarnock after "a small medical procedure" in hospital then endured a 5-1 thrashing by LASK that meant Celtic again missed out on the riches of the Champions League.

Saturday's subsequent 2-1 home win over Falkirk was hardly convincing, adding to the doubts some supporters once again have voiced about their summer transfer dealings, and assistant Shaun Maloney was sent out to meet the media instead on Tuesday.

Neverthless, they have won all five of their games apart from that collapse in Austria and go into Wednesday's meeting with Aberdeen already two points clear at the top of the table.

Similarly, counterpart Stephen Robinson has still to convince some Dons fans despite steering them clear of relegation trouble last season then starting the season with six wins and just two losses.

To make matters worse, after Sunday's home defeat by Rangers, few will be expecting much from a trip to Celtic Park, where they have not won in 14 visits.

Indeed, Celtic won all three meetings last season after Aberdeen, who have not won in 15 away league games, edged the 2025 Scottish Cup final on penalties.

Steven Pressley was not a popular choice as Dundee head coach last season, but his subsequent charm offensive means he will be forgiven quickly for a defeat by Hibernian on Sunday that ended their six-game winning run at Dens Park.

Having admitted he failed to "find the right solutions" to thwart the Leith side, Pressley now must work out how to beat St Johnstone for the first time as a manager, having lost all three meetings with the Perth side when Falkirk manager in season 2009-10.

However, other statistics are in his favour, with St Johnstone having only won one of their latest 10 meetings and Simo Valakari's side having lost three in a row on the road after Saturday's loss to Hearts and winning just one of their latest five outings overall.

Given Saturday's 4-0 home drubbing by Dundee United, it is hard to argue that Neil McCann is not the manager most under pressure.

That came after a 5-1 thrashing by Celtic in their last home league game.

A 3-2 Ayrshire derby win over second-tier Ayr United came in between that, but that is their only victory in five outings.

McCann will take heart from two wins over St Mirren since taking charge in January, a 4-3 victory at Rugby Park in February then a 3-0 success in Paisley in May.

It leaves Kilmarnock unbeaten in four meetings with the Buddies since losing on penalties in League Cup last September after 2-2 draw in Ayrshire.

Craig McLeish's side arrive having been held to a 3-3 draw by Motherwell on Sunday after a 5-1 hammering by Rangers in the League Cup.

However, until then, St Mirren had been unbeaten in five away from home, winning the latest three without conceding a goal, and will be out to prove the Ibrox capitulation was a mere blip.

Having continued the swashbuckling style imposed successfully by Jens Berthel Askou last season, Motherwell's Alfred Johansson is probably the manager least under scrutiny.

Yet the Swede's side are without a win in four after Sunday's draw with St Mirren and are also four trips away from home without a win, albeit two of those were in Conference League qualifying against HJK Helsinki and Freiburg.

Indeed, they have lost 10 goals in their latest three outings and, including the end of last season under his predecessor, they have gone five home league games without a win.

Jim Goodwin will have had a wry smile from his hospital bed considering his United side had gone three games without scoring before crushing Kilmarnock on Saturday to end run of four without a win and three straight defeats in his absence.

They also failed to score in two defeats and one draw with Well last season, losing 2-0 twice at Fir Park - and have lost all five visits since a win in April 2023.

Goodwin will hope they can alter that trend too under assistant Sharp on Wednesday.

Rangers have only lost one of their latest five outings, but amid those results they failed to qualify for either the Europa League or the Conference League.

So Sunday's win over Aberdeen, albeit it narrow, has eased some of the pressure building early into Derek McInnes' Rangers reign.

It will be lumped back on again should they fail to beat Falkirk considering John McGlynn's side are without a win in three and have lost four of their past five at home, including their latest three in the league.

Included among those are a 5-2 hammering by Rangers on the final weekend of last season, a near repeat of the 6-3 scoreline on their previous visit, leaving the Ibrox side unbeaten in six meetings since Falkirk won 3-2 in Championship in March 2016.

Both capital clubs impressed in Conference League play-offs on Thursday, albeit Hibs ultimately lost out to two late goals at home to Gent.

David Gray's side bounced back with a 2-1 win away to Dundee that means they have suffered just one defeat in their latest seven outings.

Hearts followed up their European heroics against Rapid Vienna by holding off a spirited St Johnstone comeback on Sunday and are now unbeaten in six since a 6-1 thrashing by Benfica completed an opening four defeats under new head coach Wouter Vrancken.

A 2-1 derby victory against nine men at Easter Road in April is, nevertheless, Hearts' only win in eight league games on the road.

Should they win a third derby in a row, they will have consigned Hibs to five straight home league defeats for the first time since 2010. Some incentive!

Celtic could introduce their latest signing, Oliver Sorensen on loan from Parma, but he will surely not replace Benjamin Nygren in midfield considering the Swede scored in all three of their games against Aberdeen last season.

Two Scottish midfielders who have not quite lived up to their early promise could get their chance to revive their careers in opposition at Fir Park.

Former Dundee midfielder Lyall Cameron, whose family are United fans, could make his debut for the Tannadice side on loan from Rangers.

Meanwhile, Dylan Levitt will be keen to face his former club after his arrival from Leyton Orient.

United will also have to keep on eye on Tawanda Maswanhise, with last season's top scorer getting off the mark on Sunday and having already scored five times in six Premiership appearances against the Tannadice side, including three in his last two at Fir Park.

Former Kilmarnock defender Joe Wright could face St Johnstone after his move from Bradford City to Dundee, who might also complete the signing of Manchester United midfielder Jack Moorhouse in time to play.

Meanwhile, St Johnstone are hoping to gain permission to play former Fortuna Dusseldorf midfielder Danny Schmidt.

articles.summary: Liverpool’s Lucca Brughmans Move Raises Big Alisson Questions on Transfer Deadline DayTransfer deadline day has a way of stripping away the noise and leaving...
articles.body:
Liverpool's Lucca Brughmans Move Raises Big Alisson Questions on Transfer Deadline Day

Transfer deadline day has a way of stripping away the noise and leaving the truth standing there in plain sight. For Liverpool, the truth in this case is simple enough. They have moved for one of Europe's brightest young goalkeeping prospects, and in doing so they have effectively confirmed that the club are looking beyond Alisson.

That is the nub of it. Everything else is detail, and some of that detail matters a great deal. As reported by The Athletic , Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign Genk goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans. The fee is substantial, the contract is long, and the timing tells its own story. This is not the sort of move you make on a whim. It is not the sort of cheque you write for a lad of 18 unless you believe there is a first-class goalkeeper in there somewhere.

The broad numbers underline the point. Liverpool will pay "a fixed fee of around €33million (£28.3m; $38.3m) and €2m more due in potential add-ons" for Brughmans, with the teenager returning to Genk on loan for the rest of the 2026-27 campaign. He has signed a six-year contract at Anfield. Clubs do not hand out six-year deals because they fancy a look. They do it because they are planning ahead.

Liverpool transfer strategy points to life after Alisson

The line that jumps off the page from the original report is blunt and revealing: "This is an unexpected deal for Liverpool and one that opens up plenty of questions about the future of the goalkeeping department." It does exactly that. In one stroke, Liverpool have introduced a fresh layer of intrigue around the most important position on the pitch outside the centre-forward role.

Alisson has been one of the pillars of Liverpool's modern era, a goalkeeper who has saved points, rescued performances and given calm to teams that often needed it. Yet football does not stop for sentiment, and elite clubs have to know when to prepare for change before the change becomes unavoidable. The report states, "The Brazilian is most likely playing his last season at the club and the need for a replacement is crucial." That is not idle speculation. That is the clearest indication yet that Liverpool's succession planning is now active rather than theoretical.

There is also the practical side. Alisson's quality has never been in doubt. His availability has, at times, been another matter. As The Athletic piece notes, there is "no obvious understudy for Alisson, a goalkeeper who has missed large chunks of the last few seasons through injury." That sentence cuts right to the heart of the issue. Liverpool cannot drift into a future where they are hoping rather than knowing.

For a club now under Andoni Iraola, with expectations unchanged and patience always in short supply, uncertainty in goal is not healthy. It bleeds into everything else. Defenders drop off, midfielders second-guess their press, and the whole side can start to wobble. Liverpool know this, which is why this move feels both surprising and perfectly logical.

Lucca Brughmans profile explains Liverpool interest

Brughmans is not arriving on hype alone. The report makes clear that "Lucca Brughmans is a talent already on the radar of Europe's biggest clubs, thanks to his impressive profile and recent breakthrough into the first team." At 18, he has already travelled fast. He made his professional debut for Jong Genk at 16, and last season "started all 10 of their Pro League play-off fixtures." That is proper exposure, proper pressure, proper experience for a young goalkeeper.

That matters because this is not a position where promise alone carries you. Goalkeepers have to deal in judgement, patience and nerve. Young outfield players can get away with a flashy cameo or two. Young keepers get examined under a harsher light. One flap at a corner, one poor starting position, one bad decision with the ball at their feet, and the noise begins.

Liverpool appear convinced that the tools are there. The fee says that. The contract says that. The fact that Genk had only recently tied him down until 2030 says that Liverpool have had to pay a premium because they were not buying a distressed asset. They were buying potential at a level the market already recognised.

Still, there is a dose of realism needed. The original report gets that balance right. "For all of Brughmans' talent, it would have been a gamble to throw him straight into the squad without any training, and at such a tender age." Exactly. There is no point pretending this lad is turning up next week to take the gloves and transform the place. He is "very much one for the future."

That phrase is important because supporters often want transfer business to answer every question immediately. This one does not. It answers one question in part, Liverpool are preparing for the next chapter. It leaves another hanging in the air, who will actually be trusted when Alisson goes?

Giorgi Mamardashvili uncertainty still lingers

This is where the move becomes more interesting, and perhaps a touch more unsettling. The report says Liverpool "initially hoped that player would be Giorgi Mamardashvili, but the Georgian is yet to make an impact." If that assessment is fair internally, then the club's goalkeeping roadmap is not as settled as many might have assumed.

There is a revealing line in the piece, "Like when Liverpool sensed a market opportunity for Mamardashvili in 2024, they've spotted another chance to build for the future here." That reads like a club still searching for certainty. There is nothing wrong with opportunism in the market, especially when the talent ceiling is high. But there is a difference between stockpiling options and identifying your next No 1 with complete conviction.

The article adds, "Yet it's clear by this move that they do not feel sufficiently stacked for life after Alisson so the uncertainty around the No 1 position will grow as his time at the club edges towards the end." That is the key takeaway. Liverpool have acted, but the action itself tells you the issue remains unresolved.

That may be sensible. It may even be smart. It is certainly preferable to doing nothing and waking up a year too late. But the size of the Brughmans deal also means expectations will not stay modest forever. At £28.3m rising further with add-ons, this is not a quiet little development signing to tuck away in the background. It is a major investment in a specialist position, and every appearance, every loan update and every whisper from Belgium will now be examined for clues.

As a Liverpool supporter, this report leaves you intrigued more than anything else. You can see the logic straight away. Alisson has been magnificent for years, but time waits for nobody and elite clubs have to be ahead of the curve. If Liverpool really believe Brughmans is special, then moving early makes complete sense, even at £28.3m plus add-ons.

The part that catches the eye, though, is what this says about the rest of the goalkeeping picture. If Mamardashvili was meant to be the obvious successor and "is yet to make an impact", then the club are still searching for clarity. That is not panic, but it is uncertainty. Liverpool supporters can live with a long-term plan. What they do not want is a muddled one.

There is also the emotional side of it. Alisson has been one of the defining figures of the modern Liverpool side, the sort of player who gives supporters trust. Replacing that presence is about far more than reflexes and distribution. It is about authority.

Brughmans sounds like a serious talent, and Genk is a fine place to keep developing for the season. So this feels like one to watch closely. It may look like a future move on paper, but in reality it says plenty about Liverpool's present anxieties and their next big decision.

articles.summary: Sunderland AFC have signed Belgium international winger Malick Fofana (21) from Ligue 1 side Lyon, both clubs have announced. OL have confirmed that the Blac...
articles.body:
Sunderland AFC have signed Belgium international winger Malick Fofana (21) from Ligue 1 side Lyon, both clubs have announced . OL have confirmed that the Black Cats have struck a €40m agreement with Les Gones . Sunderland will pay a €35m transfer fee, with a further €5m in add-ons. Lyon also negotiated a sell-on clause. Sunderland had been in negotiations with Lyon and the winger's representatives throughout the final stages of the transfer window.

Fofana had attracted significant interest from across the Premier League. Arsenal had explored a move but were unwilling to meet Lyon's €40m asking price, while Crystal Palace had also attempted to hijack Sunderland's deal but have ultimately come up short in their pursuit of the OL attacker, despite Pierre Sage's attempt to sway his former player towards joining Selhurst Park.

Fofana joined Lyon from Gent in January 2024 and quickly established himself as one of the club's most exciting attacking players. His departure will represent a significant loss for Lyon, who have been forced to sell the wide forward after failing to qualify for the UEFA Champions League. Fofana could make his Premier League debut against Brentford on Saturday.

articles.title: Bills stash LB who made 56 tackles for them last season on practice squad
articles.summary: The Bills brought back 32-year-old linebacker Shaq Thompson on the practice squad after he recorded 56 tackles in 12 games for Buffalo last season.
articles.body:
Shaq Thompson is back with the Buffalo Bills .

The Bills signed the veteran linebacker to their practice squad Monday after Thompson spent the entire offseason as an unrestricted free agent.

"I wanted to be a Bill. I wanted to play football. I wanted to be around these guys," Thompson said on Tuesday. "When you come to work everyday and everybody has the same mindset... They make work fun. They make the building fun. Atmosphere is fun.

"Just brothers. It's more than just football players coming together. It's a true family here."

Thompson, 32, didn't participate in OTAs, training camp or the preseason, so he'll need some time to get back into football shape.

But the Bills already know what he can do.

Thompson played 12 games with six starts for Buffalo last season and finished seventh on the team with 56 tackles despite dealing with hamstring and neck injuries. He also had six tackles for loss, one sack and a forced fumble.

Thompson stepped up in the playoffs, too. He intercepted a pass in the Bills' wild-card victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars and led Buffalo with eight tackles. He added five tackles, including two tackles for loss, against the Denver Broncos in the divisional round.

The Bills now have an experienced linebacker in case he's needed again.

Buffalo has Terrel Bernard back in the middle of its defense, but the depth behind him is young. Dorian Williams, Kaleb Elarms-Orr and Joe Andreessen are the other inside linebackers on the Bills' initial 53-man roster.

Thompson gives Buffalo insurance if one of those players struggles or an injury creates an opening.

The Bills used their practice squad last season to bring back several veterans who weren't with the team during training camp, including safety Jordan Poyer, wide receiver Gabe Davis and defensive tackle Jordan Phillips.

Thompson has a similar opportunity to work his way back into the lineup. He had to ramp up last year, too.

Thompson suffered a torn Achilles in September 2024 during his final season with the Carolina Panthers, ending his season after four games. He recovered in time to sign a one-year, $1.255 million contract with Buffalo in June 2025 and was ready for the season opener.

The Panthers selected Thompson with the No. 25 overall pick in the 2015 NFL Draft. He spent his first 10 seasons in Carolina and has 808 tackles, 13 sacks, three interceptions and five forced fumbles in 135 career games.

He played his first two NFL seasons in Carolina when Bills general manager Brandon Beane was the Panthers' assistant general manager and former Bills head coach Sean McDermott was the defensive coordinator. Those relationships helped bring Thompson to Buffalo last year.

This time, the Bills don't need him to immediately step into the lineup.

articles.title: Commanders may have found a steal in former Chiefs' offensive tackle
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders signed a former Chiefs' offensive tackle who could prove to be a steal.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have been mostly quiet over the past few days, as they finalized their initial 53-man roster and practice squad. After finalizing their roster on Sunday, Washington re-signed 12 players it had just waived or released to the practice squad.

On Tuesday, the Commanders finished filling out their practice squad, signing five players from outside of the organization. Veteran cornerback Isaac Yaidom was the most notable signing, as he could contribute immediately.

While Yiadom and fellow cornerback Terell Smith could prove to be helpful soon, there was one player who could be a steal: offensive tackle Esa Pole.

Pole, a 6-foot-7, 319-pound tackle from Washington State, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2025. After being initially waived during last summer's final cuts, the New York Jets claimed Pole off waivers. He was waived in October, and the Chiefs wasted no time bringing him back, signing him to the practice squad.

Pole was signed to the 53-man roster on Dec. 3, and he made his NFL debut at left tackle the following week. Kansas City's starting left tackle was injured on the first play, and Pole replaced him. He would then go on to start the final four games at left tackle.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid, who knows a thing or two about the offensive line, was a fan of Pole.

"Big guys are hard to find that can move like he does, and he had a decent training camp for us, and he's a young guy," Reid said last year, via Chiefs Wire .

Reid had more praise for Pole after his first NFL game.

"So after the game, I mentioned I was proud of him because he had no reps in practice for the most part and then just a couple of fill-in things. I thought he did a nice job for what he was asked to do," said Reid. "We just picked him back up here, and he again had limited reps and jumps, and I mean, he's a rookie." He jumped in and did some pretty good things against what I think is a pretty good football player."

Pole earned first-team reps for the Chiefs during OTAs, but he was surprisingly waived earlier this week during final cuts. It's unknown why Kansas City gave up on Pole, but he could prove to be a valuable addition for the Commanders.

He's a young offensive tackle who has already earned some valuable starting reps. So, if something were to happen to current left tackle Brandon Coleman, the Commanders could elevate Pole to start in a pinch. Even if Laremy Tunsil returns later this year, Washington could have a future swing tackle in Pole, which could allow Coleman to shift back inside.

Pole is not a finished product. He didn't begin playing organized football until his first year at Chabot College in 2021. He previously played basketball.

As a former basketball player, Pole is light on his feet, which should make him a fit for new offensive coordinator David Blough's zone-blocking scheme. Even if Pole doesn't play in a game for the Commanders, it's absolutely a risk worth taking.
